subject: Segmentation assertions and penetration test evidence request
body:
From: Josh Blake <josh.blake@finexus.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Finexus Security <security@finexus.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation assertions and PT evidence for Finexus private deployment

Hi David,

Thanks for the briefing last week. As part of our procurement security review we need a few artifacts specific to our private VPC deployment:

- A short mapping showing where Redwood asserts tenant/network segmentation is enforced for customer-managed private deployments (control-level, not just product pages).
- A copy or summary of the latest external penetration test that covers tenant isolation and edge proxy surfaces (we accept redacted reports).
- A simple evidence matrix mapping those items to SIG and CAIQ controls (or pointers to existing artifacts).

Preferably delivered as a zip or links to a secure drive. Can you confirm whether your private package includes any customer-facing NAT/eip that could create cross-tenant egress paths?

We are on a tight timeline—ETA by 2026-07-15 would be ideal.

Thanks,
Josh
Josh Blake
Senior InfoSec Manager, Finexus
security@finexus.com

-----
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Josh Blake <josh.blake@finexus.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation assertions and PT evidence for Finexus private deployment

Hi Josh — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Grace (Infra Eng) and Neha (Security) to pull the specific artifacts and draft the SIG mapping. A few quick clarifying questions so we send the right things:

1) Are you requesting our standard private deployment (customer VPC + Redwoods services in a dedicated VPC peered or transit-attached), or the on-premise appliance option?
2) For the PT report: redacted PDF is fine. Do you need the full report, or would a summary + findings table suffice for procurement?
3) When you say "customer-facing NAT/eip" — do you mean any ephemeral egress IPs used by the runtime (e.g., for outbound telemetry/updates) or static address ranges assigned to the deployment?

Attaching the requirements spreadsheet you mentioned for reference.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Josh Blake <josh.blake@finexus.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation assertions and PT evidence for Finexus private deployment

Josh,

Thanks — quick update and an initial artifact bundle attached. High level:

- Segmentation assertions: Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments enforce tenant isolation at three layers: network (VPC/subnet per tenant or per-customer enclave), compute (container/GPU allocation + cgroups, per-tenant allocation), and application (authz boundary at request router). See the attached "redwood-segmentation-map-v1.pdf" for the diagram and assumptions.
- Penetration testing: Attached is our latest external PT summary that includes tenant isolation validation and edge proxy testing (redwood-pt-summary-2026-04.pdf). The full report is vendor-owned; we can provide a redacted copy under an NDA if needed.
- Evidence mapping: We have a CSV with control mappings to SIG/CAIQ for segmentation controls; attaching as "segmentation-assertions-sig-mapping.csv".

Notes on NAT/egress: for the typical Private deployment we do not assign customer-facing static EIPs on the runtime by default. Outbound telemetry and OS/package updates flow through a managed egress subnet owned by the customer (customer-managed NAT or firewall recommended). In multi-tenant Dedicated pools we use NAT gateways in a controlled egress VPC and maintain IP allowlists for partner integrations.

Attachments included (stubs):
- redwood-segmentation-map-v1.pdf (diagram + boundary assumptions)
- redwood-pt-summary-2026-04.pdf (3-page summary, findings table)
- segmentation-assertions-sig-mapping.csv (control matrix)

If you want a redacted copy of the full PT or the vendor correspondence for audit, say the word and we’ll route the NDA.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-segmentation-map-v1.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]
[attachment: redwood-pt-summary-2026-04.pdf (pdf, 98KB)]
[attachment: segmentation-assertions-sig-mapping.csv (csv, 12KB)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation assertions and PT evidence for Finexus private deployment

Hi Josh — two technical clarifications to make sure the mapping meets your audit: 

- Egress model: please confirm whether your deployment will be one of the two models we documented: (A) Customer-managed VPC with Redwood runtime peered and customer NAT/egress; or (B) Dedicated Redwood-hosted pool with controlled egress and shared NAT. The artifact we provided assumes model A unless you tell us otherwise.
- SIG/CAIQ format: do you prefer a populated CAIQ matrix format (Excel) or a short narrative mapping with citations to the PT summary? Many customers prefer the spreadsheet.

Also: if you require proofs such as packet captures or firewall rules, we will need a formal request and an approved data-handling agreement—those proofs contain operational metadata that is sensitive.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Josh Blake <josh.blake@finexus.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation assertions and PT evidence for Finexus private deployment

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We are planning model A (customer-managed VPC) but will confirm the final network architecture by 2026-07-09. A spreadsheet CAIQ mapping is preferable. Redacted PT PDF + mapping by next Wednesday (2026-07-15) is acceptable.

One more ask: can you add a short column in the mapping that states whether the evidence is vendor-supplied (Redwood PT), customer-supplied (e.g., customer firewall rules), or third-party attestation? That will speed our audit.

Appreciate it,
Josh
